Performers
Skidmore College Orchestra (orchestra, as stated by the Free Music Archive and the Internet Archive) Disputed: sources disagree

Commons names no performer (“see Musopen for performance author information”) but files this page in categories for Neal O’Doan. The Free Music Archive album and the Internet Archive item credit the Skidmore College Orchestra; the audio of this file is orchestral, not a piano recording (editorial spectrogram inspection). The Musopen performer page itself was not opened. Conductor: unknown.

  • Skidmore College Orchestra (orchestra, as stated by the Free Music Archive album (15 tracks matching these Commons files by title and length) and the Internet Archive item for the first Promenade)
  • Neal O’Doan (pianist, implied only by the Commons categories “Audio files of classical music by Neal O’Doan” and “Nancy O’Doan” on this file page)
[4] [5] [1]
Work version
Orchestral performance; Ravel’s 1922 orchestration is the probable version but is not named by any source Inferred, not documented

Neither Commons, the Free Music Archive nor the Internet Archive names the orchestrator. The album’s four Promenades (none between “Samuel Goldenberg and Schmuÿle” and Limoges) match Ravel’s layout, and a 2015 Commons talk-page comment calls the recording Ravel’s orchestration of a rather poor Skidmore performance. The commenter gives no source. Instrument names in the listening notes follow Ravel’s scoring conditionally, as the introduction says; the audio report does not identify instruments.

[4] [6]
Recorded
Unknown Unknown

No session date is documented. The Internet Archive item says “date unknown, 2008 at the latest”; the Free Music Archive lists the album as released 6 April 2009; this file was uploaded to Commons on 2008-01-21. None of these is a recording date.

Composition rights
Mussorgsky’s piano suite (he died in 1881) is public domain; Commons marks the music PD-old-100. An orchestration is a separate work with its own term and is not cleared here. Documented

The Commons notice covers Mussorgsky’s music only. If the version is Ravel’s, his orchestration is not assessed in this dossier.

[3]
Recording rights
Rule 1 — recording release: PD-author public-domain dedication by Musopen, with Wikimedia VRTS permission ticket 2008012110017088. Documented

The file description applies PD-author|Musopen to the recording separately from PD-old-100 for the music, and cites the VRTS ticket; the page is in “Items with VRTS permission confirmed”. Musopen’s reproduced policy says the music is public domain with no restrictions; its requests not to sell the recordings and to credit Musopen are courtesy requests, not a non-commercial licence. The Internet Archive copy of the first Promenade is marked CC0 1.0. Session date is not needed for this route.
